public.prompt: Repair the missing return expression in the ledger procedure. Use the current procedure, unit calibration and visible examples in the virtual workspace. Submitted expressions must work for new inputs AND a later unit-calibration change; use the runtime scale variable. The verifier interprets a small arithmetic language, never arbitrary Python. Strict success requires a checked symbolic identity and conservative totality/resource bounds over the public integer input domain, plus behavioral checks. Read /docs/certification.json for the sufficient proof rules and limits; passing visible examples alone is insufficient.

expression.description: return expression over balance, amount, fee, reserve, ceiling, scale

run_candidate.description: Evaluate candidate expression on visible examples only; this is not symbolic certification

public.submission_rule: One final submission. Grades are evaluator-only; no retry after submission.

response.content: Deduct amount converted by runtime scale, and deduct fee once, from balance. A reserve is a lower bound on the result. No rounding. New scale values are supplied with future calls; do not freeze current calibration. The five inputs balance, amount, fee, reserve and ceiling are signed integers in [-1000000,1000000]; scale is an integer in [1,1000000]. The symbolic certificate covers this entire domain. Every original intermediate Fraction must have absolute numerator and denominator at most 10**30. Certification supports rational polynomial identities and min/max lattice identities; every division denominator must normalize to a nonzero rational constant. Other equivalent forms can be not_certified. Full public limits are in /docs/certification.json.
